title: Garage Door Service Call Intake Form
subtitle: Control inspection, stored-energy control, repair, balance, safety testing, and release through verified identity, domain-specific observations, evidence, authorization, exception ownership, and accountable closeout.
description: An original, workflow-complete garage door service service call intake for doors, tracks, springs, cables, operators, controls, and safety devices. It connects manufacturer information and approved safety scope to present conditions, repeatable evidence, decisions, unresolved work, and the receiving party's handoff.
use_case: Use when a garage-door service coordinator must triage and route a new garage door service request without promising scope before site, asset, hazard, access, and authorization facts are known.

sections.title: Garage Door reported condition and immediate triage
sections.guidance: Preserve the caller's facts, distinguish an active hazard from a service symptom, and assign immediate controls.

items: Door sections, joints, reinforcement, glazing, weather seal, and damage

Vertical and horizontal tracks, brackets, fasteners, alignment, and clearance
Rollers, hinges, bearings, shaft, coupler, and moving-hardware condition

blocks.guidance: Select only observations reported or directly confirmed during intake.

blocks.label: Condition timing, recurrence, and current state

items: Door, operator, remotes, and controls isolated against unexpected movement

Structural attachments, header, track supports, and fasteners assessed
Photoelectric, edge, force, reversal, release, and control functions preserved
Replacement spring, cable, roller, hardware, and operator compatibility verified

Full balance and entrapment-protection test plan completed before release

blocks.label: Dispatch and qualification assignment

items: Secure and support the door before controlled work

blocks.guidance: Verify the full intake record before arrival and stop or escalate when spring, cable, door support, operator, entrapment protection, balance, structural attachment, electrical, or controlled-energy condition is uncertain.

sections.title: Garage Door intake exception, containment, and escalation
sections.guidance: Make the trigger, immediate protection, decision owner, deadline, and dispatch restriction reconstructable.

blocks.label: Garage Door exception and stop-work indicators
items: Door, spring, cable, fixture, or counterbalance energy not controlled
Door cannot be independently supported during work
Track, header, bracket, ceiling, or structural attachment is damaged or uncertain
Cable fray, spring crack, bottom-fixture damage, or uncontrolled movement observed
Photoelectric, edge, force, reversal, or emergency-release protection fails
Door is unbalanced, binds, drifts, falls, or requires excessive manual force
Operator, wiring, grounding, control, or power condition is unsafe
People, pets, vehicles, or property cannot be kept clear of the travel path
Replacement component compatibility or manufacturer procedure is uncertain
Customer requests bypass, disabling, or release without required safety protection
blocks.guidance: Select the observed condition; do not use a generic exception when the actual trigger is known.

sections.title: Garage Door service call intake closeout and accountable handoff
sections.guidance: Close only when outcome, remaining limitation, next action, evidence, and receiving ownership agree.

blocks.label: Remaining action and follow-up register
Final outcome, handoff, and record location
Record boundary and stop condition
blocks.guidance: This garage door service service call intake is an operational record, not a substitute for applicable law, licensing, product labeling, manufacturer instructions, site policy, safety requirements, or professional judgment. Stop affected work, access, application, operation, testing, or release when spring, cable, door support, operator, entrapment protection, balance, structural attachment, electrical, or controlled-energy condition is uncertain. A garage-door safety supervisor must review the exception, authorize the controlling decision, and preserve its evidence before closeout.
